# Conformance fixture format (`conformance-v0.3.json`)

One JSON file, shared by the Node.js (`@rudderstack/ai`) and Python (`rudderstack-ai`) SDKs. Each SDK has a driver that runs every scenario and compares the events it emits with `expected`. Keys are snake_case; drivers map them to their own option names (camelCase in Node.js).

```json
{
  "fixture_version": 1,
  "spec_version": "0.3.0",
  "description": "...",
  "scenarios": [
    { "name": "...", "description": "...", "config": {}, "replies": {}, "steps": [], "expected": [], "exact_numbers"?: true }
  ]
}
```

## Per scenario

Start each scenario from a clean state: a fresh in-memory RudderStack client set as the global client, `capture_content`, `emit_llm_calls` and `tool_breakdown` from `config` (all default `false`), `identity_from_cookies` from `config` (default `true`), `redact` from `config` (default `true`: built-in masking, no hook), `azure_deployment_models` from `config` (`azureDeploymentModels` in Node.js), an empty price table, no Azure deployment mapping, and an empty reply queue on the mock LLM server. Claude session ids are unique per scenario, so the SDKs' in-process session usage map needs no reset.

### `config`

`{ "capture_content"?: boolean, "emit_llm_calls"?: boolean, "tool_breakdown"?: boolean, "identity_from_cookies"?: boolean, "redact"?: boolean, "azure_deployment_models"?: { <deployment>: <base model> }, "event_rules"?: { "tools": { <tool name>: <rule> } }, "classifier"?: { "intents"?, "outcomes"?, "classify": { "intent"?, "outcome"?, "intent_summary"? } | "throw", "delay_ms"? }, "server_feedback"?: boolean, "evaluator"?: { "scores": [<score>] } | "throw" }`, passed to `configure`.

A tool rule is an event name (string) or `{ "event", "properties_args"?, "properties"?, "when"? }`, mapped to a real rule as follows: `properties_args: [keys]` is `properties(args, result) = { key: args[key] for each key }` (a missing key is sent as absent, not null); `properties: "throw"` raises instead; `when: "never"` returns false; `when: "throw"` raises. Without `event_rules` there are no rules.

`classifier` is passed as `configure(classifier={classify, intents, outcomes})` (no client or model: the scenarios classify with a deterministic `classify` function). `classify` as an object means `classify(turn)` returns exactly those fields (`intent_summary` as `intentSummary` in Node.js); `"throw"` means it raises. With `delay_ms`, the function returns its result (or raises) after that many milliseconds (Node.js: a promise; Python: an async function when a loop runs, otherwise it sleeps in the worker). Without `classifier`, classification is off.

`server_feedback` (default `true`) is `configure(serverFeedback)` / `server_feedback`. `evaluator` is an evaluator function that returns exactly the listed scores for every turn (each score's keys snake_case: `evaluation_name`, `score_value`?, `score_label`?, `evaluator`, `sampled`?, `explanation`?; camelCased in Node.js), or raises with `"throw"`. Without `evaluator`, evaluation is off.

### `replies`

Exact provider replies, queued per route and served in order, one per request:

| Route                | Endpoint                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `openai.chat`        | `POST /v1/chat/completions`                                                                                                                 |
| `openai.responses`   | `POST /v1/responses`                                                                                                                        |
| `anthropic.messages` | `POST /v1/messages`                                                                                                                         |
| `google.generate`    | `POST .../models/<model>:generateContent` (Gemini API `/v1beta/models/...`, Vertex AI express mode `/v1beta1/publishers/google/models/...`) |
| `google.stream`      | `POST .../models/<model>:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`                                                                                     |

Each reply is one of:

- `{ "status"?: number, "headers"?: { <name>: <value> }, "json": any }`: a JSON body (`status` defaults to 200), with those extra response headers (a gateway's `x-litellm-response-cost`, `x-litellm-model-name`).
- `{ "status"?: number, "headers"?: { <name>: <value> }, "sse": [{ "event"?: string, "data": any }] }`: a `text/event-stream` body; each entry becomes `event: <event>\ndata: <data>\n\n`, with `data` JSON-encoded unless it is a string (`"[DONE]"`).
- `{ "hang": true }`: accept the request and never answer (the client times out or aborts).
- `sse` with `"hang_after": true`: send the listed events, then keep the connection open without ending it (the client aborts or times out mid-stream).

Replies are complete and fixed; drivers must not rely on any default mock behaviour. Chat streams always end with a usage chunk (`choices: []`), as the API does when `stream_options.include_usage` is set; the SDKs request it on every host.

### Clients

Provider clients point at the mock (`OPENAI_BASE_URL` = `<mock>/v1`, Anthropic and Google Gen AI base URL = `<mock>`), use any API key, and have **retries disabled** (`maxRetries` / `max_retries` = 0; the Google Gen AI clients do not retry by default). The `google.vertex.*` calls use a Vertex AI client in express mode (`vertexai: true` with an API key and no project), so no Google Cloud credentials are needed. LangChain steps use a `ChatOpenAI` on the same mock, or a `ChatAnthropic` with `provider: "anthropic"`.

Run in order. Ops:

Option keys: `user_id`, `anonymous_id`, `conversation_id`, `feature`, `intent`, `trace_id`, `input_method`, `prompt_text`, `trigger`, `account_id`, `on_behalf_of`, `trigger_source`, `task_name`, `parent_interaction_id`, `tool_breakdown`, `cookies` (a `Cookie` header string or a name-to-value map, passed as is), `identity_from_cookies`, `classify`, `surface`, `trigger_event_id`, `attachment_count`, `attachment_types`. Every message is consumed. Inside an `interaction` it reports into it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

### Bedrock calls

`bedrock.converse` and `bedrock.converse_stream` run against an in-memory fake Bedrock Runtime client (no mock server), wrapped with `wrapBedrock` / `wrap_bedrock`. The fake answers from the step:

- `params`: the Converse request (`modelId`, `messages`, `toolConfig`, ...), with the same field names in both SDKs. Node.js sends it as `client.send(new ConverseCommand(params))` / `new ConverseStreamCommand(params)` (the fake receives the real command objects); Python calls `client.converse(**params)` / `client.converse_stream(**params)`.
- `response` (`bedrock.converse`): the Converse output body, returned as is.
- `stream` (`bedrock.converse_stream`): the event objects the response's `stream` yields, in order (`messageStart`, `contentBlockStart`, `contentBlockDelta`, `contentBlockStop`, `messageStop`, `metadata`), each as the SDKs yield it (`{ "contentBlockDelta": { "contentBlockIndex": 0, "delta": { "text": "..." } } }`).
- `request_id`: the AWS request ID on the response: Node.js `$metadata.requestId`, Python `ResponseMetadata.RequestId`. Without it the response has none.
- `error`: `{ "code", "status", "message" }`: the call raises instead of answering. Node.js: `new <code>({ message, $metadata: { httpStatusCode: status } })` with the SDK's exception class of that name (`ThrottlingException`, `ValidationException`, ...). Python: `botocore.exceptions.ClientError({"Error": {"Code": code, "Message": message}, "ResponseMetadata": {"HTTPStatusCode": status}}, "Converse")` (`"ConverseStream"` for the stream API).
- `stream_error`: `{ "code", "message" }`: raised while iterating, after the listed `stream` events, as the SDKs raise modeled stream exceptions. Node.js: `new <code>({ message, $metadata: {} })` thrown from the async iterator; Python: `botocore.exceptions.EventStreamError({"Error": {"Code": code, "Message": message}}, "ConverseStream")` raised from the iterator.

## `expected` and normalisation

`expected` lists every track call the scenario must produce, in emission order. Before comparing, normalise each emitted message to:

```json
{ "event": "...", "userId"?: "...", "anonymousId"?: "...", "properties": {}, "context": {} }
```

- Keep only `event`, `userId`, `anonymousId` (omit when unset or null), `properties` and `context`. Drop every other envelope field (`messageId`, `timestamp`, `originalTimestamp`, `sentAt`, `type`, `integrations`, ...).
- `context`: drop `library`; in `context.wrapperLibrary` drop the top-level `name` and `version` (each SDK sends its own) and keep `specVersion` and `integration`; a nested outer `wrapperLibrary` is kept as is.
- IDs minted by the SDK are UUID v4 strings. An `interaction_id` or `parent_interaction_id` that is a UUID v4 becomes `$int1`, `$int2`, ... (one shared map; within an event `interaction_id` is mapped first) and a `conversation_id` that is one becomes `$conv1`, ..., numbered in order of first appearance within the scenario. Other (caller-supplied) IDs are compared literally.
- `latency_ms`, `time_to_first_token_ms`, `tool_duration_ms` and `classifier_duration_ms`, when present with a number >= 0, become `"<number>"`; so do `duration_ms` and `max_duration_ms` in each `tool_breakdown` entry. Present vs absent still matters.

Then compare:

- Objects by key set and values; key order is ignored. A missing or extra key is a difference.
- Arrays by length and position.
- Numbers by value with a relative tolerance of 1e-9 (`0` equals `0.0`); with `"exact_numbers": true` on the scenario, numbers must be exactly equal.
- Everything else strictly.

Each emitted event must also validate against `spec/ai-events-v0.3.schema.json` (the drivers' usual schema check); a declared tool event (a name not starting with `ai_`, carrying `tool_status`) against `$defs/declared_tool_event`.

## Rules the expected events encode

- No `spec_version` property: every event carries `context.wrapperLibrary.specVersion: "0.3.0"` on the SDK's own level.
- Minted `interaction_id` and fallback `conversation_id` values are UUID v4; the SDK never invents an `anonymousId` when a `userId` is set (`ai_system` only when there is no identity).
- Every `usage_breakdown` entry has `total_tokens` (input + output).
- `reasoning_tokens` (per call and per `usage_breakdown` entry) and `total_reasoning_tokens` are provider-reported reasoning tokens, a subset of output tokens (never added to them again, never more than them). A reported `0` is sent; a provider or call that reports no count (Bedrock, an Anthropic response without `output_tokens_details`, a failed call) has no field, never an estimate or `0`. Anthropic: `usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens` (Messages API extended thinking; already inside `output_tokens`, the last streamed value wins); Claude Agent SDK: `modelUsage[model].thinkingTokens` (already inside `outputTokens`; a turn delta like the other counters, split over a model's agents in proportion to their output tokens; absent on CLI versions that do not record it, and then no field), and an entry or answer has one when at least one of its calls reports a count (the sum of those).
- Google Gen AI: input = `promptTokenCount` (which includes `cachedContentTokenCount`) + `toolUsePromptTokenCount`; output = `candidatesTokenCount` + `thoughtsTokenCount`, and `thoughtsTokenCount` is also `reasoning_tokens`; so input + output = `totalTokenCount`. `cachedContentTokenCount` is `cached_input_tokens`. Streamed `usageMetadata` is a running total: the last value wins, never a sum. Tool calls come from the `functionCall` parts (Gemini reports `STOP` for them too). `finish_reason` is normalised as for Bedrock: `STOP` is `stop` (`tool_calls` when a part calls a function), `MAX_TOKENS` is `length`, the safety, recitation, blocklist, prohibited-content and SPII reasons are `content_filter`, and so is a blocked prompt (`promptFeedback.blockReason`, a success with no candidates); other values pass through. Provider `gcp.gemini` (Gemini API) or `gcp.vertex_ai` (Vertex AI), the OpenTelemetry `gen_ai.provider.name` values every integration sends, priced separately (see Prices).

- The last model call decides the status: a failed final call gives `response_status: error` (or `timeout` / `cancelled`) and its `error_type`, even after earlier successes; a successful retry is a success. An error raised out of the interaction sets the status from that error.
- The held `ai_user_prompt_created` is sent when the first model call starts: an intent set before that is on it, one set during or after the first call only on `ai_response_received`.
- Empty strings for `user_id`, `anonymous_id`, `conversation_id` and `feature` (interaction and `track_action` options) are absent: the context's value applies.
- `primary_model` / `primary_provider`: the last successful call; when no call succeeded (an error, timeout or cancelled answer), the last attempted call.
- A stream closed before it completed (`break`, abort) is a cancelled call: `error_type: cancelled`, tokens seen so far, no `cost_usd`; the answer is `cancelled` when it was the last call.
- Cost precedence: a cost the provider, gateway or framework reported wins (OpenRouter and the LiteLLM proxy's `usage.cost`, else the LiteLLM proxy's `x-litellm-response-cost` header; a number, or a decimal string such as `"1.5e-05"`; null, blank or negative is no cost), then a registered price, otherwise no cost.
- No cost the SDK does not know: failed and cancelled calls carry no `cost_usd` (unless a framework reported one) and add nothing to totals; a priced `0` is sent. `total_cost_usd` (and an entry's `cost_usd`) is the sum of the priced calls, sent only when at least one call is priced and every successful call is.
- A failed Responses API response keeps its usage; its per-call event has `finish_reason: failed` and `error_type: api_error`.
- `finish_reason` uses Chat Completions' terms on both OpenAI APIs: a completed Responses API output with only tool calls (no message) is `tool_calls`; `incomplete` with `max_output_tokens` is `length` (other reasons as sent, e.g. `content_filter`); a refusal (Chat `message.refusal`, a Responses `refusal` content part) is `refusal`; a streamed Chat refusal keeps the wire's `finish_reason`.
- A completed call is a success whatever its `finish_reason`: a refusal, a content filter, or output cut off at `length` (structured or not) is billed and returned, so it is visible through `finish_reason`, not through `response_status`. Only an exception the app gets fails the answer: the OpenAI parse helpers throwing `LengthFinishReasonError` / `ContentFilterFinishReasonError` give `response_status: error` with `error_type` `length` / `content_filter`, and the call keeps its usage and price.
- A non-streamed Responses API request with `background: true` is only queued: it passes through untracked (no call, and no interaction of its own).
- Streamed chat requests carry `stream_options.include_usage` on every host; a request the host rejects with HTTP 400 or 422 that names the parameter or carries no error code is sent once more as the app wrote it, and only that request is recorded. A coded rejection (a content filter, a prompt too long) is never resent.
- An error is mapped through retry and framework wrappers to the error that caused it (`lastError` / `cause`; Python: tenacity `last_attempt`, `__cause__`, then the implicit `__context__`).
- A call seen by two wrappers (a client wrapped twice) is recorded once: a failed call by the first wrapper that sees the error, and a repeated response adds no tool calls.
- LangChain: a model run's usage is the sum over its prompts (the first generation of each); chunk usage adds up, as LangChain merges chunks; a cancelled or aborted model run keeps the usage streamed so far (unpriced). A retriever run attaches like a chain run: a root retriever run owns its answer. A tool run inside another tool run (a Deep Agents subagent inside `task`) has that enclosing tool as `parent_tool` in `tool_breakdown`, unless run metadata `parent_tool` names one. A Gemini model's (provider `gcp.gemini` / `gcp.vertex_ai`) own finish reasons map as for Google Gen AI (`STOP` `stop`, `MAX_TOKENS` `length`, the safety and other blocked reasons `content_filter`), read from `response_metadata.finish_reason`, else the generation info's `finish_reason` / `finishReason`.
- `tool_call_count` counts every tool the model invoked, including Anthropic `server_tool_use` / `mcp_tool_use` and Responses API `*_call` items.
- Gateways and routers (shared table: `spec/fixtures/providers-v0.1.json`): a call through `openrouter`, `litellm` or `gateway` whose model has a vendor prefix (`openai/gpt-4o`) is reported under that vendor (`openai`), with the full name in `model`. The served model is the response's `model`, or the LiteLLM proxy's `x-litellm-model-name` header when present (its body `model` is the alias the app asked for). `requested_model` is the request's model, sent on `ai_llm_response_received` and `usage_breakdown` entries only when the served model differs from it beyond a vendor prefix or version suffix (`gpt-4o` served as `openai/gpt-4o-2024-08-06` sends none). Bedrock's `[region.]anthropic.` prefix and `-v<n>:<n>` suffix, and Vertex's `@<date>` (read as `-<date>`), are the same model as Anthropic's ID (`us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` or `claude-haiku-4-5@20251001` served as `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` sends none). A streamed chat completion's final usage chunk may carry one choice with an empty delta that repeats `finish_reason` (OpenRouter): it is the same call's finish, not another one.
- Prices: a registered name prices a model with exactly that name, or that name followed by a version suffix (dates `-YYYY-MM-DD` / `-YYYYMMDD`, `-NNN` / `-NNNN`, `-v<n>[.<n>]`, `:<tag>`, `@<version>`, `-latest`, in any sequence), never another model of the family (`gpt-4o` does not price `gpt-4o-mini`). A model with a vendor prefix also matches by the name after its last `/` (`openai/gpt-4o-2024-08-06` as `gpt-4o`; the full name wins a tie). A provider-specific price matches only its provider and the labels naming the same service: `gcp.gemini` and its alias `google` (the Gemini API), `gcp.vertex_ai` and its alias `google.vertex` (Vertex AI), so a price registered under an alias prices the calls; the Gemini API and Vertex AI never share prices. The longest matching name wins, then a price for the call's own provider, then one for a same-service label, then a generic one; `configure(prices)` merges. Costs are rounded half-up to 8 decimals. `cache_write_1h_per_mtok` prices Anthropic 1-hour cache writes (`cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`), defaulting to `cache_write_per_mtok`.
- Cloud model IDs: for provider `aws.bedrock` the model is matched as sent, then without a leading inference-profile prefix (`us.`, `us-gov.`, `eu.`, `apac.`, `jp.`, `au.`, `in.`, `global.`), then without its vendor prefix (up to the first `.`: `anthropic.`, `amazon.`, ...); the longest registered name wins, then a provider-specific price, then the earlier (more literal) form. No other provider has prefixes stripped. Vertex `claude-...@<revision>` matches through the `@<version>` suffix. For provider `azure.ai.openai` a deployment name in `azure_deployment_models` is priced as its base model; events keep the deployment name; nothing is inferred without a mapping.
- Bedrock Converse: `input_tokens` = `inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheWriteInputTokens` (AWS `inputTokens` excludes the cache), `cached_input_tokens` = `cacheReadInputTokens`, cache writes priced at `cache_write_per_mtok`; streams take usage only from the `metadata` event. `finish_reason` from `stopReason`: `end_turn` / `stop_sequence` → `stop`, `tool_use` → `tool_calls`, `max_tokens` → `length`, `guardrail_intervened` / `content_filtered` → `content_filter`, anything else as sent. `response_id` is the AWS request ID, `model` the request `modelId`. A stream that ends without `messageStop` is a failed `api_error` call. A failed stream call (an exception while iterating, or no `messageStop`) keeps the `response_id` and counts the tools seen so far; it ends an interaction the wrapper opened itself, never one the app opened. Error types: a name or code containing `throttling` is `rate_limit`, `accessdenied` `auth_error`, `validationexception` `invalid_request` (case-insensitive), otherwise the HTTP status decides as for other providers.
- LangChain outside an interaction: the handler opens a `user`-triggered interaction (prompt event included) with identity from run metadata; `agent_name` from `agent_name` / `lc_agent_name` metadata or an `agent:<name>` tag.
- Claude Agent SDK `modelUsage` rows whose model has no assistant message and ran no subagent (a subagent tool result's `resolvedModel`) in a tracked stream are internal CLI bookkeeping calls: they do not contribute to `llm_call_count`, tokens, cost or `usage_breakdown`. The primary model's row is always kept. A turn with a subagent whose model is unknown, and standalone result mapping (no message stream), keep every reported row.
- Background fields (`account_id`, `on_behalf_of`, `trigger_source`, `task_name`, `parent_interaction_id`) are on every event of an interaction when set (`ai_user_action`: `account_id`, `on_behalf_of`), never null or empty, and SDK-owned: extra properties with those names are ignored. `account_id` / `on_behalf_of` fall back to the context.
- `aiTask`: `trigger: system`, no prompt event, never the enclosing `userId` / `anonymousId`. Without `parent_interaction_id` it chains to the current interaction (and takes its `conversation_id`); an explicit one wins (no conversation inherited); `null` opts out. `trigger_source` defaults to `agent` whenever there is a parent. Otherwise `conversation_id` is minted (the context's is not used).
- `tool_breakdown` (opt-in) is one entry per agent/MCP server/tool/parent combination, built from the same de-duplicated calls as `tool_call_count`, so the `call_count`s sum to it. Flat `mcp__server__tool` names split into `mcp_server` and `tool_name`; unnamed calls are `unknown`.
- `error_count` counts known failures. `error_types` uses only `rate_limit`, `timeout`, `cancelled`, `denied`, `auth_error`, `invalid_request`, `connection_error` and `api_error`; unknown categories become `api_error`, never raw messages.
- `duration_ms` sums measured durations even with partial coverage; `measured_count` is that coverage and `max_duration_ms` the maximum. Nested durations with `parent_tool` are inclusive.
- Entries sort by `agent_name`, `mcp_server`, `tool_name`, `parent_tool` (absent sorts as empty), in UTF-16 code-unit order. An explicit `mcp_server` wins over the one in an `mcp__server__tool` name; `error_type` only categorises a call that failed (`error: true`). A tool span without a provider ID completes an earlier call of the same tool and MCP server whose agent and parent tool match or are unknown on either side.
- Claude Agent SDK attribution: a subagent's messages (`parent_tool_use_id` set) take the `subagent_type` input of the `Task` / `Agent` call that launched them (else the message's own `subagent_type`, which the Python SDK does not expose); main-loop messages have no `agent_name`. Their tools carry that `agent_name` and `parent_tool`, the launching call's tool name when it was seen. A finished subagent's last call (its answer) is not streamed: when the launching call's tool result (`tool_use_result`) carries `usage`, that call counts as one more call of the subagent on its `resolvedModel` (unless its input side equals the subagent's last streamed message, the same call). Each model's turn totals are split over its (agent, loop) groups: as observed when they add up; else the main loop keeps `result.usage` (exact) and the other groups share the rest, when none of it goes negative; else each token kind in proportion to what was observed (largest remainders); the model's cost is split by Claude price ratios (input 1, cache read 0.1, cache write 1.25, output 5), the last group (the main loop when present) taking the rest, so entries always add up to `modelUsage`. A query that neither resumes nor continues a session never treats its first result as cumulative.
- OpenAI Agents SDK: one run is one interaction (it joins an active one). Every model response is one call attributed to the agent that made it (`agent_name`), with the agent's configured model name; a nested run of an agent used as a tool reports the model name from its trace span. `finish_reason` is `stop` for a completed response; a response cut off at the output-token limit (Responses `status: incomplete` with `incomplete_details.reason: max_output_tokens`, Chat Completions `finish_reason: length`) is `length`, never the raw `incomplete` status, and keeps its usage even though the Agents SDK raises on the Responses case; the run is then `response_status: incomplete` with `error_type: length`, as for other providers (Chat `content_filter` is kept as sent). Model-requested tools (function, hosted, handoffs as `transfer_to_<agent>`) are tool calls; a local function tool's execution adds its outcome (the Agents SDK's "An error occurred while running the tool." output is a failure) and duration. A guardrail tripwire is `response_status: error` with `error_type: guardrail_trip`. A provider error fails the call in flight and the run; calls before it keep their usage. The session ID is the `conversation_id` unless one is given.
- Bedrock: a call's tool outcome comes from the `toolResult` block a later request in the same interaction sends back (`status: "error"` is a failure).
- Identity from cookies (RudderStack JavaScript SDK v3): `rl_anonymous_id` → `anonymousId`, `rl_user_id` → `userId` (fallback only: not when any explicit or context `user_id` or `anonymous_id` is set), the `rl_session` object's `id` → `context.sessionId` (a number; `sessionStart` is never sent; none when its numeric `expiresAt` is in the past). Explicit interaction options > `aiContext` values > cookies. Unreadable cookies are skipped. `identity_from_cookies: false` (global, or per interaction, which wins) ignores cookies, also for a `track_action` inside that interaction. `aiTask` never reads cookies.
- Opt-in text (`prompt_text`, `response_text`, `action_details.feedback_text`) is masked by the built-in patterns by default, exactly as `spec/fixtures/redaction-v0.1.json` specifies (`[email]`, `[phone]`, `[card]`, `[ip]`, `[secret]`, `[ssn]`, `[iban]`); text over 32000 code points is withheld (not sent). `redact: false` sends it unmasked.
- `ai_user_action`: `action_details` is omitted when nothing is left in it (for example only a `feedback_text` that capture is off for).
- Declared tool events: one track event per tool call of a tool with a rule, named by the rule, at most once per call (the same de-duplicated calls as `tool_call_count`). It is sent as soon as the call is settled (its outcome, or an output without an outcome, is seen: an Anthropic `tool_result`, an OpenAI `role: tool` message or Responses `*_call_output` item in a later request of the interaction, a LangChain tool end/error), otherwise when the interaction ends, just before `ai_response_received`. Properties: the rule's `properties()` output first, then the interaction's IDs and background fields, `trigger`, `agent_name` (when the call has one), `tool_name`, `tool_call_id` (the provider's ID; absent for calls without one, such as a LangChain tool run without a tool call), `tool_status` (`success` / `error` from the outcome, else `unknown`) and `tool_duration_ms` (measured only, rounded; never `0` with `unknown`). SDK-owned names in `properties()` output are dropped. `when()` false or raising sends nothing; `properties()` raising sends the event without custom properties, and so does `properties()` output that takes the event's properties over the 30,000-byte budget (serialized JSON, UTF-8), which otherwise applies to every event, `mcp_*` included: over it, captured text goes first (`response_text`, `prompt_text`, `action_details.feedback_text`), then `tool_breakdown` and `usage_breakdown` entries from the end. Arguments and results are never sent otherwise.
- Intent classification (`classifier` configured): each interaction that ends with `response_status: success` and has classification on sends one `ai_interaction_classified`. On by default only for interactions the app opens itself (`aiInteraction` / `startInteraction`) with `trigger: user`; off for `aiTask` unless the task option `classify: true`, and off for interactions an integration opens on its own (a call outside any interaction, a LangChain handler run, a Claude query turn) unless that integration is given `classify: true`; the interaction option `classify: false` opts out. It is sent after its `ai_response_received`, never before and never blocking it. Properties: the interaction's IDs and background fields, `trigger`, `intent` (the classifier's value when it is one of `intents`, any non-empty string when no `intents` are configured, else `other`), `outcome` (one of `outcomes`, default `resolved`, `partial`, `unresolved`, `unclear`; else `unclear`), `intent_summary` (from `classify` whenever it returns one; from a model client only with `intent_summary: true`; masked like other text, then whitespace collapsed, cut to the first sentence, at most 25 words and 280 characters (code points), and withheld when it still matches a pattern or masking fails), `classifier` (`custom` for `classify`, `model` for a model client), `classifier_model` (model only), `classifier_duration_ms`, `classifier_cost_usd` (model only, when priced; never added to `total_cost_usd`). A raising or timed-out classifier, or an unparseable reply, sends nothing.

## MCP rules

The fixture steps cannot drive an MCP server, so these rules are written here and each SDK's own MCP tests cover them.

- `call_index` counts the reported `mcp_tool_called` events of a scope (`mcp_session_id`, else a caller-sent `interaction_id`) from 0, with no gaps. On 2026-07-28 a `tools/call` answered with `resultType: "input_required"` sends no `mcp_tool_called`; it takes the scope's next position, and the retry that carries `inputResponses` for one of its elicitations keeps that position (`call_index` and `ms_since_previous_call`) instead of taking a new one, and has no `retry_count`. A call, then an elicited call: `call_index` 0, then 1 (never 2). A retry whose `input_required` leg this process does not know (expired or answered elsewhere) is counted as a new call.
- `mcp_event_delivered`: a delivery without a `subscription_id` or an `event_id` (absent, not a string, or empty after trimming) sends nothing and logs one warning per process; the app's sender still runs and its result or error is returned unchanged. It is never sent with `unknown` for either ID. `mcp_event_subscription_changed` likewise sends nothing without a `subscription_id` or `event_name`.

# Cookie fixture format (`cookies-v3.json`)

Generated by `scripts/generate-cookies-fixture.mjs` with `@rudderstack/analytics-js-cookies`; both SDKs must reproduce it exactly.

- `values[]`: `{ name, description, raw, decoded }`. `raw` is a cookie value as it appears in a `Cookie` header. Decoding: URL-decode it (`decodeURIComponent`; invalid percent-encoding or invalid UTF-8 → unreadable, and `+` stays `+`); an empty result is unreadable; with the `RS_ENC_v3_` prefix, base64-decode the rest (Node's `Buffer` rules: missing padding is fine) to UTF-8; then `JSON.parse`. Any failure gives `null`.
- `identities[]`: `{ name, description, cookies, expected }`. `cookies` is a header string or a name-to-value map. A header splits on `;`; each segment splits on its first `=`, name and value trimmed; segments without `=` or with an empty name are skipped; a repeated name keeps the last value. Map values are decoded the same way. `expected` has `anonymous_id` / `user_id` when the decoded value is a non-empty string, and `session_id` when `rl_session` decodes to an object whose `id` is a positive integer number (a safe integer).
